title: STADA secures exclusive ensartinib distribution rights across 14 MENA markets | HealthCare Middle East & Africa - No.1 Health & Pharma Manufacturing Industry Publication
summary: STADA MENA will also purchase finished ensartinib capsules from Xcovery, which will remain responsible for manufacturing and supply.
thbAction: Use the article as an entry point to pitch THB's commercial visibility layer for territory planning, account prioritization, and next-best-action for pharma leadership teams.
contentHtml:
GERMANY—STADA Group has entered into a licensing and supply agreement with Xcovery Holdings, a subsidiary of China’s Betta Pharmaceuticals, to commercialize the lung cancer treatment ensartinib across 14 Middle East and North Africa (MENA) markets.

Under the agreement, STADA MENA DWC LLC will receive exclusive rights to market, import, promote, distribute, and sell ensartinib hydrochloride in Saudi Arabia, Lebanon, Jordan, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Iraq, Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, Egypt, and Libya.

Xcovery will receive an undisclosed upfront payment and potential milestone payments.

STADA MENA will also purchase finished ensartinib capsules from Xcovery, which will remain responsible for manufacturing and supply.

Expanding access to targeted lung cancer treatment

Ensartinib is a next-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) inhibitor developed by Betta Pharmaceuticals and Xcovery for patients with ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

China approved the treatment in November 2020, followed by regulatory approvals in the European Union, the United States, and Macao Special Administrative Region.

The partners are preparing marketing authorisation applications across the MENA region, with STADA expected to lead local commercialisation activities.

STADA Executive Vice-President of Emerging Markets Stéphane Jacqmin said the agreement complements the company’s existing specialty medicines portfolio in the region, which includes oncology treatments such as trabectedin and bortezomib.

He added that the partnership strengthens STADA’s position across specialty pharmaceuticals, generics and consumer healthcare in MENA markets.

Partnership combines regional reach and manufacturing capabilities

Betta Pharmaceuticals Assistant Chairman Shizhe Ding said the agreement represents another step in the company’s international expansion strategy.

He highlighted the growth potential of the ALK-targeted therapy market in the Middle East and North Africa, noting that STADA MENA’s knowledge of local pharmaceutical markets complements Xcovery’s research, manufacturing and supply capabilities.

Xcovery Chief Executive Officer Li Mao said clinical studies had demonstrated ensartinib’s efficacy and safety in patients with ALK-positive NSCLC.

He added that the company would use its global quality management and manufacturing systems to maintain a reliable supply of finished capsules to STADA MENA.

The agreement reflects a broader strategy among pharmaceutical developers to expand access to oncology medicines through regional licensing partnerships rather than establishing independent commercial operations in every market.

For STADA, the deal adds a targeted cancer therapy to its specialty medicines business, while Betta Pharmaceuticals gains a regional commercialisation partner with established market knowledge and distribution capabilities.

The arrangement also places responsibility for manufacturing and product supply with Xcovery, allowing the partners to divide operational and commercial responsibilities as they pursue regulatory approvals across the 14 markets.
